# Reconstruct Embedding from a Wavelet Band-Interval

<div>

> **Note**
>
> `fbands='all'` is equivalent to `fbands=[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]` when the
> `Wdecomposition` onbject has been created with a wavelet transform of
> level 8. Using `fbands='all'` reconstructs the full signal from all
> subbands.

</div>

``` python
from nbdev_fhemb.decomposeEmb_ex import percentile_emb_decomp
```

``` python
percentile_emb_decomp.create_wreconstruction( # reconstruct a signal from specified frequency bands (fbands)
    subjs=[(40, 42), 50],                     # Subjects to project the reconstruction for: may be specified as intervals, e.g., [(40, 42)]
    fbands='all'                              # frequency bands to include in the reconstruction (default is 'all')
).features_tint['subj40']
```

<div>

> **Note**
>
> Using `fbands = []` disables wavelet-based reconstruction and returns
> the original (undecomposed) input signal unchanged.

</div>

<div>

> **Warning**
>
> Returning the original (undecomposed) input signal bypasses the
> wavelet pipeline entirely. Consequently, the output includes all
> features of the original embedding - including components that were
> projected out during decomposition. For this reason, the returned
> signal is comparable to a wavelet-based reconstruction only after
> re-projecting its features into the same embedding subspace.

</div>

``` python
percentile_emb_decomp.create_wreconstruction( # reconstruct a signal from specified frequency bands (fbands)
    subjs=[(40, 42), 50],                     # Subjects to project the reconstruction for: may be specified as intervals, e.g., [(40, 42)]
    fbands=[]                                 # frequency bands to include in the reconstruction (default is 'all')
).features_tint['subj40']
```

<div>

> **Caution**
>
> The original (undecomposed) signal and the fully reconstructed signal
> are not perfectly identical. Small differences arise from boundary
> handling, finite-precision arithmetic, and other numerical effects in
> the wavelet transform.

</div>

``` python
percentile_emb_decomp.create_wreconstruction( 
    subjs=[(40, 42), 50],              
    fbands='all'                    
).features_tint['subj40'] - percentile_emb_decomp.create_wreconstruction(
    subjs=[(40, 42), 50],                 
    fbands=[]                           
).features_tint['subj40'][[0,10,18]]  # We have to re-project the features into the embedding space of the reconstruction
```
